metadata.summary: Luke Littler beat rival Luke Humphries to win on his return to the European Tour at the Czech Darts Open in Prague.
metadata.content: Czech Darts Open: Luke Littler topples Luke Humphries 8-6 in final on return to European Tour in Prague | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to content Czech Darts Open: Luke Littler topples Luke Humphries 8-6 in final on return to European Tour in Prague Littler beats Humphries 8-6 in final after beating Michael van Gerwen, Danny Noppert and Krzysztof Ratajski earlier on Sunday; Sky Sports remains the home of darts with the World Grand Prix coming up from September 28-October 4 Sunday 6 September 2026 23:20, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Luke Littler claimed the Czech Darts Open with a win over Luke Humphries. Luke Littler beat rival Luke Humphries to win on his return to the European Tour at the Czech Darts Open in Prague. Littler had not played in a European Tour event since March, but roared to glory with an 8-6 victory in Sunday night's final to end his opponent's hopes of winning this title for a third straight year. Littler hit five 180s and averaged just over 95 as both players struggled in the heat at the PVA EXPO after a long day which had already seen The Nuke overcome Michael van Gerwen in the semi-finals, Danny Noppert in the quarter-finals and Krzysztof Ratajski in the last 16. messages.text: Great Britain and Ireland claim historic win in Walker Cup thriller

metadata.summary: Great Britain and Ireland won the Walker Cup for the first time since 2015 after a nerve-shredding late comeback saw them beat the USA by a  13½-12½ scoreline.
metadata.content: Walker Cup: Great Britain and Ireland produce stunning late comeback to beat USA 13½-12½ in thrilling contest | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to content Walker Cup: Great Britain and Ireland produce stunning late comeback to beat USA 13½-12½ in thrilling contest USA missed four putts to retain the trophy after whitewashing Great Britain and Ireland in the morning foursomes; Watch the first round of the Amgen Irish Open live on Sky Sports Golf, with coverage starting on Thursday September 10 from 1:30pm Sunday 6 September 2026 22:53, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from day two of the Walker Cup held at the Lahinch Golf Club in County Clare, Ireland Great Britain and Ireland won the Walker Cup for the first time since 2015 after a nerve-shredding late comeback saw them beat the USA by a 13½-12½ scoreline. Dean Robertson's side looked to be heading for defeat at Lahinch after suffering a clean sweep of defeats in the Sunday morning foursomes and with the Americans three points ahead going into the singles matches. But the home side lost only two of the 10 matches and the competition eventually came down to the very last as Josh Hill won the 18th hole of his match with Tyler Watts to seal an incredible victory. The USA will be left to regret the late turnaround after four missed putts to retain the Walker Cup. metadata.content: Lewis Hamilton claims there are 'no rules' at Ferrari after clash with team-mate Charles Leclerc during Italian GP | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Lewis Hamilton claims there are 'no rules' at Ferrari after clash with team-mate Charles Leclerc during Italian GP Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc made contact on the first lap of the Italian Grand Prix before the Brit ran onto the gravel and lost several positions; Hamilton fell 76 points behind championship leader Kimi Antonelli after the Mercedes driver came from 19th on the grid to win at Monza Sunday 6 September 2026 20:06, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martin Brundle and Nico Rosberg debate who was at fault for the collision between Hamilton-Leclerc. Lewis Hamilton has accused Ferrari of having "no rules" after a clash with his team-mate Charles Leclerc during the Italian Grand Prix. Hamilton launched an aggressive move up the inside of his team-mate at the first corner, but was then forced off onto the gravel himself on the exit of the chicane as Leclerc held onto the inside line. Hamilton dropped from his starting position of fourth to 10th, and was left playing catch-up for the rest of the race, as he eventually finished sixth. Russell led Antonelli, who stormed through the field from 19th to be in the lead battle after just 13 laps, by one second when a race-changing Virtual Safety Car was called with 25 laps remaining. Mercedes pitted Antonelli, but not Russell, for new medium tyres, which put the team-mates 15 seconds apart when the VSC ended.
